case_title: Siddaling v. The State, through Kalagi Police Station
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498-A; IPC s.306 (finally upheld). Trial court also convicted under IPC s.304-B r/w s.34, s.306 r/w s.34 and Dowry Prohibition Act ss.3, 4, 6; High Court acquitted on the other offences.
evidence_type: Oral testimony of family witnesses (victim's father, mother and two brothers); documentary evidence (panchayat agreement dated 22 June 2002)
confession: Admission recorded in the panchayat agreement dated 22 June 2002 that the accused was living with another woman; relied on by the Supreme Court
aggravating_circumstances: Suicide within four months of marriage; accused continued the relationship after the panchayat agreement; suicide within three months of the panchayat
trial_court_outcome: Accused convicted under IPC ss.498-A, 304-B r/w 34, 306 r/w 34 and Dowry Prohibition Act ss.3, 4, 6; sentence for the trial court not separately stated
high_court_outcome: Appeal partly allowed: conviction under ss.498-A and 306 IPC maintained; acquitted of other offences; co-accused father acquitted of all charges
offence_finally_established: IPC s.498-A (cruelty); IPC s.306 (abetment of suicide)
neutral_facts: The victim was married to the accused and, within four months of the marriage, died by jumping into a well in the village. The prosecution alleged that the victim took this step because of harassment over an alleged dowry demand and cruelty, the accused being involved in a relationship with another woman. The prosecution relied on oral evidence from the victim's father, the victim's mother and two brothers, each of whom stated that the accused had a relationship with another woman. A further document was produced: an agreement executed before a village panchayat dated 22 June 2002, in which the accused admitted living with another woman, and which was seen by the victim. Under that agreement the accused agreed to sever the relationship and to live with the victim at the victim's house. The witnesses stated that the accused continued the relationship after the agreement, which, according to the prosecution, caused mental agony to the victim. The victim died within three months of the panchayat meeting.
physical_harm: Death of the victim by suicide (jumped into a village well)
number_of_offences: 7 charged (IPC ss.498-A, 304-B, 306; Dowry Prohibition Act ss.3, 4, 6); 2 finally upheld (IPC ss.498-A and 306)
motive: Accepted by the Court: the accused's continued relationship with another woman caused psychological imbalance and mental agony to the victim, leading to suicide
key_evidence_accepted: Oral testimony of PW-1, PW-6, PW-10 and PW-22 that the accused continued his relationship with another woman; panchayat agreement dated 22 June 2002 recording the accused's admission
witness_credibility: Court relied on the consistent statements of these four family witnesses; no specific credibility analysis recorded
trial_duration: offence: 17 September 2002; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 27.06.2007; Supreme Court: 09 August 2018
legal_representation: Accused: Girish Ananthamurthy and Mrs. Vaijayanthi Girish, Advocates. State: Joseph Aristotle S. (senior counsel) and Ms. Anitha Shenoy, Advocates
investigation_status: Trial completed with conviction; FIR and charge sheet not described in the judgment
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted on multiple counts. High Court: partly allowed; conviction under ss.498-A and 306 IPC maintained, other offences acquitted. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld and sentence not reduced
defence_argument: No mens rea or active/direct act inciting suicide, so s.306 not made out (relying on Gurucharan Singh); plea for leniency in sentence
legal_principle_applied: Abetment involves a mental process of instigation or aiding; facts must be carefully assessed to decide whether cruelty induced the victim to commit suicide; the accused's illicit relationship could create psychological imbalance negating s.306 defence
precedent_relied_upon: Randhir Singh v. State of Punjab (2004) 13 SCC 129 (relied on for abetment); Gurucharan Singh v. State of Punjab (2017) 1 SCC 433 (cited by the appellant)
sentencing_rationale: Suicide within four months of marriage and within three months of the panchayat made leniency misplaced; not a fit case to reduce the sentence
judicial_aggravating_factors: Suicide within four months of marriage and within three months of the panchayat convened over the accused's relationship
